summary: Walter Yeeling Evans-Wentz worked in religious studies, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford University (~1903–1907), the University of Oxford (1907), Jesus College (~1907–1910), and under traditional teacher Kazi Dawa Samdup (~1919–1922).
Walther Schubring was an Indologist who studied under Ernst Leumann (~1903–1906). He later served as a professor at the University of Hamburg (attested 1958).

Walther Wüst was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1920–1923), where he later served as rector from 1941 to 1946.
Wang Pachow worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology. He studied under Yun-shan Tan and served on the teaching and research staff at Visva-Bharati University.

Wannaporn Rienjang is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of Cambridge. She held posts at the British Museum, the University of Oxford (attested 2019–2022), and Thammasat University (attested 2022–2023).
Warren Cowgill was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He studied at Stanford University (~1948–1952) and Yale University (~1952–1957), and held a post at Yale University in 1956.

Warren Lee Todd is a scholar in philosophy and Indology who completed his PhD at Lancaster University (attested 2012) under doctoral supervisor Chakravarthi Ram-Prasad. He also studied under Irina Kuznetsova, Chogye Trichen Rinpoche, and Peter Harvey.

Warrin Ratanamalai is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University under supervisors Phra Suthithammanuwat and Phra Srisitthimuni, having also studied under Phra Sudhivorayan and Phramaha Somjin Sammāpañño.

Wasu Harada works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Ryukoku and Koyasan universities, he held posts at Koyasan University (attested 1992), Ryukoku University (attested 1999–2006), Kyushu Ryukoku Junior College (attested 2002–2007), and Shuchiin University (attested 2006).

Wataru S. Ryose is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison by 1987 under Minoru Kiyota, having also studied under Genjun Sasaki and Frances A. Wilson.

Wayne Proudfoot is a scholar of philosophy and religious studies. He studied at Harvard Divinity School (~1962–1965) and Harvard University (~1965–1972), and held a post at Columbia University from around 1972 to 2018.

Wei Lin is an archaeologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Nanjing University, Peking University, and Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Her career includes posts at Nanjing Municipal Museum and Transylvania University (attested 2007).

Wei-jen Teng works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy. He studied at the University of Chicago and Harvard University (PhD attested 2011) under Robert M. Gimello and Parimal G. Patil, later teaching at Dharma Drum Institute of Liberal Arts.
Weirong Shen is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. He held teaching posts at Renmin University of China (~2006–2015) and the University of Hong Kong.
Weiru Guan is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).
Wen-ling Jane is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She completed a PhD at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Robert A. F. Thurman and also studied under Lobsang Jamspal.

Wenbiao Mai is an Indologist and linguist who studied at Peking University (PhD), the University of Hamburg, and Kyoto University. He held an appointment as a visiting assistant professor at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2013).

Wendi L. Adamek specializes in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and religious studies, completing a PhD at Stanford University in 1998. She held positions at Barnard College (attested 2008) and the University of Calgary (attested 2018).

Wendy Doniger is an Indology and religious studies scholar. She studied at Radcliffe College, Harvard University under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and the University of Oxford, before serving as a distinguished professor at the University of Chicago from ~1978.
Wenjie Duan was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the Central Academy of Fine Arts (~1940–1943) and served as director of the Dunhuang Academy in 1991.
